{{Short description|Mathematical theory}}
In [[set theory]], the '''random algebra''' or '''random real algebra''' is the [[Boolean algebra]] of [[Borel set]]s of the unit interval modulo the [[ideal on a set|ideal]] of measure zero sets. It is used in '''random forcing''' to add '''random reals''' to a [[model (model theory)|model]] of set theory. The random algebra was studied by [[John von Neumann]] in 1935 (in work later published as {{harvtxt|Neumann|1998|loc=p. 253}}) who showed that it is not isomorphic to the [[Cantor algebra]] of Borel sets modulo [[meager set]]s. Random forcing was introduced by {{harvtxt|Solovay|1970}}.
